subject: Exportability & training eligibility — quick verification
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Eliot Harper <eliot.harper@brightline.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Exportability & training eligibility — quick verification

Eliot,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Before we finalize the SOW I wanted to confirm two small but important points for procurement/legal on your side:

1) Will Brightline permit Redwood to use Brightline customer interaction data for model improvement? Our standard opt-in is to allow aggregated, de-identified usage to inform future model updates. If you require a no-training commitment we can provide an addendum and operational controls (ephemeral KV, onshore-only processing, explicit retention windows).

2) For exportability and audits: can you confirm whether you need SFTP exports of raw transcripts or if API-based exports (paged JSON over a secure channel) suffice? If you require SFTP we can provision an onshore SFTP endpoint and a documented retention SLA.

If you can confirm those two points (and whether legal would prefer language we proposed in the redline we shared), I’ll loop in legal and get a formal addendum drafted.

I'll attach the redline we referenced in our meeting for convenience.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed-no-train-addendum.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Eliot Harper <eliot.harper@brightline.health>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightline.health
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exportability & training eligibility — quick verification

Sean,

Appreciate the clear summary — helpful.

Short answers:
- Training/model improvement: At this stage Brightline requires a no-training commitment for any PII or patient-identifiable transcripts. We are open to aggregated telemetry for platform health (e.g., anonymized latency/error metrics) but not content-derived model updates.
- Exports: Procurement prefers SFTP exports for the first 6 months of the pilot for our internal QA, then switch to API pulls. SFTP must be hosted in our US region (us-east-1) and meet our retention policy (90 days on SFTP).

I'll attach our security FAQ and procurement checklist. Legal will review once Redwood provides proposed addendum language; procurement can't sign off until we have that.

Thanks — happy to walk the redlines live if that helps.

— Eliot
Head of Platform & Integrations
Brightline Health

Attachment: brightline-security-faq.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Sep 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Exportability & training eligibility — suggested redlines

Sean / Marissa —

See Eliot's responses below. Procurement is clear about the SFTP requirement and Brightline needs a hard no-train commitment for PII/patient transcripts.

Suggested next steps from legal:
- Provide a short addendum titled "No-Training & Export Controls" that (a) disallows use of Brightline customer content for model training or improvement; (b) documents operational controls (ephemeral KV, explicit KV TTL, onshore-only processing for flagged data); (c) includes an onshore SFTP export SLA (90-day retention, encrypted at rest) and an acceptance test.
- Limit the addendum scope to the pilot (60 days) and include a renewal clause for production.

I've prepared a redline with language we typically use for healthcare pilots — attached. If you want I can remove any clause that would require infrastructure changes and convert them to operational commitments.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

Attachment: legal-redline-no-train.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

Eliot,

Thanks — that's clear and helpful. Attached is a short addendum draft we use for healthcare pilots. Key points:
- Explicit no-training for PII and session transcripts; permitted telemetry restricted to platform health metrics (latency, error rates) and strictly aggregated.
- Operational commitments: ephemeral KV TTL of 24 hours for conversational state flagged as PHI; onshore processing for flagged files; SFTP endpoint in us-east-1 with 90-day retention; sample acceptance test steps.
- Pilot scope: 60 days, with an automatic review before production.

Would you and procurement be available for a 30-minute call Monday to walk the redline? If that's good, I'll drop a DocuSign link once we have final wording.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
